name: Caffeine
aliases: caffeine, caffeine anhydrous, anhydrous caffeine, 1,3,7-trimethylxanthine, theine, guaranine, cafeína, teína, guaranina
what_is: Caffeine is a stimulant of the nervous system. It is naturally present in coffee, tea, guarana and other plants, and it is also added to energy drinks, soft drinks and some foods. The theine in tea and the guaranine in guarana are the same substance under another name. It temporarily increases alertness, reduces the feeling of tiredness, and delays and shortens sleep, especially when taken in the afternoon or evening.
why_botia: In girls, boys and adolescents the safe limit is much lower, because it is worked out per kilo of body weight rather than per person. WHO recommends reducing intake during pregnancy above 300 mg a day, because a high intake is associated with pregnancy loss and low birth weight. And in perimenopause and postmenopause, higher intake was associated with more bother from hot flushes.
can_1: Detect caffeine and common explicit ingredient names such as caffeine anhydrous when they appear in the ingredient list.
can_2: Explain how caffeine affects sleep and alertness, and show the Woman information layer.
cannot_1: Calculate total caffeine from the ingredient list when the amount is not declared there.
cannot_2: Infer the exact caffeine dose from coffee, tea, guarana, cocoa or another caffeine-containing ingredient.

sources.label: WHO 2016 — Recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience

title: Caffeine
description: Caffeine is a stimulant present in coffee, tea and guarana and added to energy and soft drinks; theine and guaranine are the same substance. In children and adolescents the safe limit is much lower because it goes by body weight, and WHO recommends reducing intake in pregnancy above 300 mg a day.
